answer: A hollow is one fake identity. The onyx is a hardware-host registry: admitting a hollow needs a fresh attested host, and that host burns pigment equal to the number of identities now anchored there. The kth hollow costs k pigment, so $n$ clones cost $n(n+1)/2$ sequentially and $n^2$ in one batch, since a host attests only its own hollow. Call this hardware-host population burn. It breaks if one host can attest several clones or if the onyx prices arrival order instead of current anchored population.
